# Standard forward-integration qualification

Base: v4 main `2e1cc19975a5c812223a19be06b9976f57444504`, after PR #417. Scope: #289 and its typed handoff to #306. MATLAB public behavior and existing saved files remain backward compatible. No v5 checkout or released package snapshot is edited.

## Evidence design

The integration slice enumerates six configurations and five execution profiles (30 support rows). Existing method/configuration fixtures supply exact source witnesses. Six richer representative scenarios fill the audited gaps: constant-hydrostatic CFL RK4, constant-nonhydrostatic RK23, and RK45 on Barotropic QG, Stratified QG, Hydrostatic and Boussinesq. These are six newly executed compositions per provider, not 30 newly executed complete trajectories. The catalog distinguishes source coverage, fresh execution and inherited evidence.

Three isolated agents own C++ method/complex-state tests and a test-only stop launcher; MATLAB continuation qualification; and catalog/schema/validator/generated support documentation. The coordinator owns integration, CI routing/artifacts, source-consumer qualification and final review. MATLAB execution is serialized, and C++ builds use separate temporary directories. No agent publishes independently.

The representative models must evolve unconstrained coefficients and particle/tracer state, retain a fixed coefficient, use two independently restartable output destinations and dense saved values, and exercise whole, segmented, MATLAB-to-C++, C++-to-MATLAB and controlled-stop continuations. Generic method-order, rejection, controller and allocation evidence remains in focused C++ tests. Historical family reports retain their original method/workload/source provenance. Inherited #417 performance evidence is usable only when its measured production sources remain unchanged; it does not become a fresh #289 timing run.

## C++ method and extension evidence

Reviewed agent commit `db42b2ef44fe633b8202590882f1b3086f3078c0` is integrated as `7e0115aa`. Both focused Release and ASan/UBSan tests pass (2/2 in 0.54 and 1.26 seconds). RK4 global convergence ratios are 17.3957 and 16.682; RK23 ratios are 8.66854 and 8.32717. The cubic continuous extensions approach a local error ratio of 16. A registered integrator-owned required complex block is the only evolving component and drives 10/3/1 adaptive rejections for RK23/RK45/RK78. Stop/resume preserves the uninterrupted trajectory exactly; owning typed-record reconstruction creates independent layout, state and controller storage. Three repeated cycles for each method retain identical storage after diagnostic/dense warmup. This explicitly does not claim MATLAB serialization of an arbitrary custom class. `.github/ci-evidence/issue-289-cpp.json` preserves measured observations and source/executable hashes.

## Integration gate

Local qualification and combined evidence checks are recorded below. Required hosted CI remains the merge gate, including source export/package verification and one documentation/production-analyzer check. No MATLAB documentation source changed; website generation is not repeated locally. Optional Full CI is not an extra gate. Hosted results and the merge commit will be recorded in the GitHub handoff.

## Findings during representative qualification

The arbitrary smooth full-grid tracer exposed a C++ vertical derivative mismatch. With `Nz=9` and antialiasing, MATLAB retains five vertical modes in `diffZF`, while C++ differentiated additional unretained modes. The original full-grid exponential tracer differed by approximately `1.74e-6` after 120 seconds; segmented runs agreed with uninterrupted C++ and hybrid differences scaled with the C++ interval. The existing C++ unit oracle also encoded the wrong full-grid vertical expectation. Reviewed correction `25f68a1a870791ab5adba56bad8113f11d50c7bd`, integrated as `a776f879`, applies retained `Nj` projection only to the vertical derivative. Sixty analytic retained/omitted-mode controls preserve full-grid horizontal derivatives; the regression fails before the correction and passes afterward in Release and ASan/UBSan. MATLAB code, fixture and tolerances remain unchanged. This production change invalidates blanket reuse of prior performance qualification; fresh matched performance and consumer checks are required.

The newly considered legacy SQG/Hydrostatic/Boussinesq evidence classes have seven failures because their historical reports predate additions to current shared test classes. The failing condition is exact test-inventory equality, before new numerical conclusions. Follow-up #418 records the required historical/current scope separation. These three classes were already omitted from ordinary CI routing and remain outside the new registration; their reports are explicitly historical workload inputs, not current readiness. The new forward-integration validator and committed execution gate remain strict. Barotropic evidence and the shared qualification catalog pass and are newly registered.

The unchanged constant-hydrostatic fixture passes after the tracer correction: all six continuation directions and two destinations pass, tracer and particle endpoint differences are zero, and the maximum saved relative error is `1.278e-15`. Eighteen actual interior coefficient records preserve the held amplitude exactly. The accepted-step stop requested at 21 seconds drains to the complete checkpoint at 37 seconds. These are development confirmation results; the final uniform-source reference/native campaign remains the committed qualification.

Source-selection and repository-scope tests pass 5/5 after the corrected kernel hash and retained integration guide were recorded. The local analyzer harness initially required no findings at all; inspection found only nine pre-existing `PROP` property-name style messages, which the repository policy explicitly classifies as nonblocking. No stable code was refactored to remove them, and passing tests were not repeated. The small direct MATLAB cubic test confirms Barotropic QG default spline extrapolation (`395.84375`) differs from explicit zero fill (`0`); the shared 3D sampler uses the latter. MATLAB issue #419 tracks the periodic small-grid behavior without changing MATLAB in this increment.

The particle-only discrepancy was a second C++ mismatch, rather than an integrator defect. A four-cell periodic shift on the six-point y grid places the second query beyond the last grid knot. The generic constant-stratification service already matched MATLAB zero fill; the shared variable-stratification adapter instead clamped to the last node. Barotropic QG also clamped, but its MATLAB override uses default cubic extrapolation. Reviewed commit `2ae8eaa32e820aa5042f62b5eaefc969254bdf94` preserves each MATLAB convention with four lines of zero-fill guarding in the shared variable adapter and removal of the BQG fraction clamp. Fixed/moving/event zero-fill controls and an independent shifted-cubic extrapolation oracle fail on old code and pass after correction. Four focused suites pass Release (1.16 seconds) and ASan/UBSan (2.25 seconds); the generic service is unchanged. No MATLAB production code changed.

The current ATS consumer was rebuilt after both production corrections, and all seven tests pass again (13.01 seconds). The final receipt records the corrected production source tree, current consumer commit and rebuilt executable hashes while retaining a note of the superseded initial check. No ATS code or dependency changes were needed.

## Final representative and evidence qualification

The committed MATLAB test `b59498d904a68509ab915e47bf908ed4c3e13450` (integrated as `6d063156`) ran against immutable native-capable runner/probe binaries built at C++ commit `2ae8eaa32e820aa5042f62b5eaefc969254bdf94`. Both providers pass all six configurations: 12 rows and 144 continuation/destination comparisons in 259.19 seconds. Maximum errors are `2.067e-15` coefficients, `1.123e-15` fields, `1.554e-15` tracers, `2.640e-15` saved values and `1.819e-12 m` particle positions. Held coefficients remain exact across 216 actual off-step records. Minimum evolution is `0.001562` coefficients, `0.2327 m` particle motion and `8.125e-5` tracer change. All controls and established tolerances are retained. The detailed fixture-development ledger is `.github/planning/issue-289-matlab-verification.md`.

The collector retains all twelve original case fragments and assembles separate reference/native receipts. Every recorded production/test source hash matches the integrated checkout, including the corrected tracer and sampler sources. The receipts preserve the distinct original MATLAB test and C++ build commits; matching file hashes establish integration equivalence without relabeling execution. All eight combined catalog/receipt methods pass, including exact source/artifact validation, deterministic generation and rejection of incomplete, mixed, failed or contradictory evidence. All newly authored MATLAB files have zero analyzer findings.

The measured reference class cost is 151.45 seconds; CI uses a 165-second scheduling estimate instead of the default 60 seconds. This changes placement only. All 38 Python CI tests pass after the final scheduling change. Existing passing Barotropic evidence and shared qualification-catalog tests are registered; legacy drift remains explicitly tracked under #418.

## Final matched performance

With other agent jobs finished and no competing scientific process observed, one excluded warmup pair followed by eight alternating measured pairs compared the pre-correction v4 production runner with the final immutable native runner. All six benchmark input hashes match the established #417 fixtures. Each measured run performs 64 accepted RK4 steps and 256 RHS evaluations including scheduled output. Runtime changes are -0.316% constant, -0.028% Hydrostatic and +0.179% Boussinesq. Maximum retained-memory increase is 0.00347%; all pass the 3% budget. This is fresh measurement after the two production corrections, not inherited #417 timing.

Numeric readback covers 43, 55 and 65 variables. Maximum normalized differences are `4.483e-16`, `5.737e-16` and zero, with matching shapes and finite/NaN/infinity masks. No successful performance gate was repeated. Exact samples, source/build provenance and input/output hashes are retained in the final qualification summary.
